Text Labels from Table Rows

Source: R/figure-data.R
PlotDataLabels.Rd

PlotDataLabels() writes one text per row with FormatTemplate() (for example titles such as "{cells:%.0f}k cells; {area:%.0f} mm2"), after optional per-column scaling. PlotDataCollapse() writes every row and joins the results into one text, for example to list patients with their cell counts in a figure note.

Usage

PlotDataLabels(data, template, id = NULL, scales = NULL, into = "text")

PlotDataCollapse(
  data,
  template,
  sep = "; ",
  order_by = NULL,
  decreasing = FALSE,
  into = "text",
  n_name = "rows"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

template

Template (see FormatTemplate()).

id

Optional columns of data kept in the output of PlotDataLabels().

scales

Named list: column to a multiplier applied before formatting.

into

Name of the text column.

sep

Separator of the collapsed rows.

order_by

Optional column to sort by before collapsing (stable, increasing).

decreasing

Sort decreasing.

n_name

Name of a column with the number of rows collapsed.

Value

PlotDataLabels(): a data frame with the id columns and into; PlotDataCollapse(): a one-row data frame.

See also

Other plot-data builders: PlotDataBindRows(), PlotDataConstant(), PlotDataCount(), PlotDataCrossShares(), PlotDataDirection(), PlotDataDominant(), PlotDataFromArrays(), PlotDataJoin(), PlotDataKeyColours(), PlotDataLonger(), PlotDataMembership(), PlotDataPairRatio(), PlotDataProduct(), PlotDataQuantiles(), PlotDataRankRows(), PlotDataRatio(), PlotDataRecode(), PlotDataRelative(), PlotDataSelect(), PlotDataShares(), PlotDataSummarise(), PlotDataUnite()

Examples

d <- data.frame(p = c("p3", "p1"), n = c(27081, 1450), g = c("A", "B"))
PlotDataLabels(d, "{n:%.0f}k cells, {g}", id = "p", scales = list(n = 0.001))
#>    p         text
#> 1 p3 27k cells, A
#> 2 p1  1k cells, B
PlotDataCollapse(d, "{p}, {n|comma}", order_by = "n")
#>                    text rows
#> 1 p1, 1,450; p3, 27,081    2
